notes.text: The supplied notice includes footnote marker [1], but its footnote text is missing. The translation of the notice is retained; completion of the source note remains unresolved.

The whole supplied body and all three English versions/notes/root decisions are retained. Abba and Mar in the heading and the full Rav Ashi in both heading and cross-reference remain literal; the pointer SEE THE ENTRY Mar bar Rav Ashi does not admit an identity merger or add the target biography's content. Sotah38b is only the conventional reading of supplied לח:, not newly verified against a named whole passage this wake. Marker [1] remains present and its actual footnote text remains absent; neither the complete short body nor this review supplies the missing source note. All old notes remain exact and this qualification is appended. p001 stays held, with no footnote invention, canonical repair, publication or semantic admission.

Hyman’s printed notice (vol. I, p. 57) contains the Sotah citation and the cross-reference. The supplied [1] comes from a Wikisource editorial note directing readers to the discussion page (“See the talk page”). The discussion reports the shorter reading Mar bar Rav Ashi for Oxford 2675. This is the discussion’s report of the manuscript. In the consulted Davidson Sotah 38b, Abba Mar bar Rav Ashi addresses the question about people to the sides of the priests. His proof from sprinkling continues onto 39a. In the cross-referenced printed entry (vol. III, p. 898), Hyman quotes the longer name and proposes reading “Mar bar Rav Ashi said, ‘Thus said my father.’” This is Hyman’s proposed reading.
